scan.summary: This is a vendor's certificate showing that all 14 portable fire extinguishers at the Portland facility got their annual maintenance on August 20, 2025, and all 14 passed. It proves the 2025 service happened. It does not cover 2026: the certificate itself says the next annual maintenance was due August 20, 2026, and that date passed about 40 days ago. Two units (W-3 and L-1) also need six-year work before November 2026, and the CO2 unit L-1 appears to be overdue for its hydrostatic test.
scan.freshness_note: This certificate is about 13 months old (service date 2025-08-20). The next annual maintenance was due 2026-08-20. If Rose City Fire Protection (or another vendor) already did the 2026 service, get that certificate and file it. If not, the annual maintenance is overdue and should be booked now.

scan.confidence_notes: The document is clear and fully readable. I read every date, unit and result directly. Because this is a vendor's service certificate, I list conditions instead of judging it for gaps. The status 'expired' is based on the due date the certificate itself prints (2026-08-20), compared with today (2026-09-29). I cannot tell whether a 2026 service has already happened and just isn't on file. Two points are my own reading of the rules and are marked inferred: (1) Under 29 CFR 1910.157 Table L-1 and NFPA 10 Chapter 8, CO2 extinguishers are hydrostatically tested every five years, so L-1 (last tested 2020) looks overdue since 2025. The vendor did not flag this. (2) The six-year internal maintenance rule applies to stored-pressure dry chemical units, not CO2, so the vendor's 'November 2026' six-year date for L-1 looks misapplied. It may really mean the hydrostatic test. Ask the vendor to confirm both points. I believe Oregon OSHA adopts 29 CFR 1910.157 through its Division 2 rules, but I did not confirm the exact OAR number. The 'due_on' dates for the November 2026 work (2026-10-31), the 2027 six-year units (2027-12-31) and L-1's hydrostatic test (2025-12-31) are my best reading of month-only or year-only entries. The monthly-inspection deadline has no single due date and should be null; a text error got into that field.
